implementation_steps.1 versioned policies per brain: delivered in brain-api: retrieval (ranking, items), graph (edge budget), injection (packing, tokens) and synthesis (tokens per call) per revision
implementation_steps.2 separate concurrency and token budgets: delivered: inference_concurrency and inference_tokens_per_minute enforced separately
implementation_steps.3 shared inference behind scoped keys an: not verified in this repo: each brain holds its own INFERENCE_API_KEY and the gateway is expected to enforce that key's limits; brain-api enforces only its own brain's budget under the declared ceiling

compatibility: Without BRAIN_POLICY_FILE every context field is unchanged and brain_policy reports source environment; ranking and packing still follow BRAIN_RANKING_POLICY and BRAIN_CONTEXT_PACKING. /instance gains brain_policy; existing fields unchanged.
rollback_rehearsal: test_c_reverting_a_revision_invalidates_only_that_instance_cache restores the previous revision and its earlier pack exactly without touching vault or graph content; removing BRAIN_POLICY_FILE returns to the environment behavior (test_without_a_policy_file_the_environment_behavior_is_kept).
limitations: Budgets and caches are per brain-api process; replicas of one brain do not share a budget.
The sum of brains' ceilings against the shared backend is not enforced in this repo; it depends on gateway key limits.
brain-ops tick synthesis keeps BRAIN_LLM_MAX_TOKENS and is not yet under the policy budget.
A refused classification call falls back to regex classification; it is visible only in budget usage counters.
The two-process fixture does not drive an inference call, so cross-brain budget isolation rests on per-process budgets.
The policy document is read on every request.
